sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Sector breadth remains narrow with only 2 of 11 groups all-green, led by Technology and Energy, while rate-sensitive sectors continue to lose ground.

Technology and Energy dominate top-tier momentum, supported by all-green performance across all timeframes in Technology (0.867 momentum) and Communication Services (0.600 momentum). Healthcare is showing upward rotation, rising to rank 5 with a strong 0.750 momentum score alongside modest 1-spot rank improvements in Communication Services and Consumer Defensive.

Meanwhile, defensives and yield-sensitive spaces are fading. Utilities holds the weakest profile in the market with a 0.067 momentum score, falling 1 spot alongside Real Estate (0.267 momentum) and Financials (0.550 momentum). Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom of the table at rank 11 with weak 0.217 momentum.

## Strength
- Only 2 of 11 sectors maintain all-green status across week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD: Technology (momentum 0.87) and Communication Services (momentum 0.60).
- Technology (0.867 momentum, rank 2) and Energy (0.783 momentum, rank 1) hold the highest absolute momentum across the board.
- Healthcare reinforces the upper tier, holding momentum of 0.750 at rank 5.

## Movers & Momentum
- Communication Services, Consumer Defensive, and Healthcare were the sole gainers over the past 5 sessions, each improving their positioning by +1 spot.
- Financials (-1 to rank 6), Real Estate (-1 to rank 8), and Utilities (-1 to rank 10) were the primary decliners over the 5-day window.
- The absolute momentum laggards are anchored by Utilities (0.067), Consumer Cyclical (0.217), and Real Estate (0.267).

## Divergences
- Industrials shows a stark divergence between its high YTD ranking (rank 4) and sub-par momentum score of 0.383.
- Communication Services holds an all-green multi-timeframe profile despite sitting at a low rank 9 (momentum 0.600).
- No fragile all-green early-warning signals are currently detected among the qualified leaders.

sectors.watchlist: - Technology - Watch for sustained outperformance vs SPY following an RS cross; confirmed if relative strength maintains its upward trajectory above the crossover point on above-average volume, and invalidated if relative strength rolls back below the benchmark line.

risk_radar.relative_strength: Technology is the sole sector genuinely beating the S&P 500, posting an rs_score of 1.00 and rs_confirmed of 1.00 while outperforming SPY across 7/7 timeframes and registering a fresh positive RS cross. Other sectors show significantly weaker confirmation despite nominal outperformance, with Energy beating SPY on 4/7 timeframes (rs_score 0.67, rs_confirmed 0.22) and Basic Materials beating on 4/7 timeframes (rs_score 0.50, rs_confirmed 0.17).
risk_radar.risks:
* Technology represents heavily crowded, isolated leadership as the only sector with full confirmation (rs_score 1.00, rs_confirmed 1.00), leaving overall market breadth narrow.
* Energy exhibits a fragile setup, with its unconfirmed rs_score of 0.67 (beating SPY on 4/7 timeframes) collapsing to an rs_confirmed of just 0.22 due to directional inconsistency.
* Basic Materials and Healthcare display weak momentum persistence, where nominal rs_scores of 0.50 (beating SPY on 4/7 and 3/7 timeframes, respectively) both fade to low rs_confirmed readings of 0.17.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Broad market leadership remains narrow with only 18 of 144 groups all-green, led by sustained strength in energy, shipping, and healthcare tech while coal and uranium suffer sharp short-term rollbacks.

Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing and Marine Shipping continue to anchor the top of the market with momentum scores of 0.993 and 0.957, respectively. Concurrently, healthcare-related groups are seeing rapid inflows, led by Diagnostics & Research surging 26 rank spots alongside Health Information Services.

Conversely, energy sub-sectors are diverging: while refining leads, extractive fuel groups are unwinding fast, headlined by steep weekly drops in Coking Coal and Uranium. Select defensive areas like Grocery Stores are beginning to flash early turnaround signals despite lower absolute momentum scores.

## Strength
- **Narrow leadership footprint:** Only 18 of 144 industry groups are all-green across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, YTD).
- **Core momentum anchors:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.993, rank 2 YTD) and Marine Shipping (momentum 0.957, rank 4 YTD) remain the premier sustained leaders.
- **Durable multi-month performance:** Diagnostics & Research (0.906), Consumer Electronics (0.910), Health Information Services (0.84), Steel (0.869), Insurance - Reinsurance, Silver, and Software - Infrastructure all maintain sustained top-36 ranks across 1, 3, and 6-month windows.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Accelerating gainers:** Diagnostics & Research led short-term advances (+26 spots to rank 44, momentum 0.91), followed by Health Information Services (+19 spots to rank 39, momentum 0.84) and Drug Manufacturers - Specialty & Generic (+17 spots to rank 79, momentum 0.64).
- **Sharp rank drops:** Coking Coal plummeted 41 spots (rank 96, momentum 0.41), accompanied by Uranium (-24 spots to rank 98, momentum 0.24) and Business Equipment & Supplies (-21 spots to rank 68, momentum 0.48).
- **Bottom-tier momentum:** Mortgage Finance (0.077, rank 142 YTD) and Airports & Air Services (0.105, rank 140 YTD) sit at the absolute bottom of relative strength.

## Divergences
- **Fading leaders:** Multiple groups with elevated momentum are seeing 5-day rank slip, including REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.68, -2 spots), Banks - Diversified (momentum 0.67, -2 spots), Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.65, -2 spots), and Utilities - Regulated Water (momentum 0.63, -4 spots).
- **Emerging laggards:** Rapid short-term rank improvements are appearing in low-momentum groups, driven by Grocery Stores (+11 spots, momentum 0.46), Real Estate - Development (+10 spots, momentum 0.41), and Aerospace & Defense (+7 spots, momentum 0.38).
